figure_candidates.label: Figure 10
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 10. (A) The biosynthetic pathway of (−)-asperpentyn (2). (B) Structures of the enantiomeric pair of epoxyquinols and
epoxyhydroquinones characterized in this study. (C−D) Proposed catalytic mechanisms of wild-type AtyD with substrates 6 and 8, respectively.
(E) AtyD_F97A mutant with 8. The wild-type AtyD cannot accommodate 8 for C-1 ketoreduction due to steric hindrance caused by residue
Phe97 interacting with the 1,3-enyne moiety of 8. In contrast, the AtyD_F97A mutant permits substrate flipping, enabling the conversion of 6 into
8, followed by subsequent S-selective C-1 ketoreduction to produce 17.
